topic.angle: Ranking pages by the number and quality of links to them

panels.text: A search engine has to decide which page to show first. PageRank was Google's way of ranking web pages.
It counts the number and quality of links to a page, as a rough estimate of how important the page is.
The assumption: more important websites are likely to receive more links from other websites.
The name is a pun. It comes from both the term "web page" and co-founder Larry Page. Today it is not the only algorithm Google uses.

probes.question: What does PageRank count to estimate a page's importance?
options: The number and quality of links to it
How long the page has existed

probes.question: True or false: PageRank is named after both the term "web page" and co-founder Larry Page.

claims.claim: Assumption: more important sites receive more links
